analysis.title: From panic to squeeze: gold
key_insights: Gold squeezed sharply higher after a positioning washout: five consecutive weeks of speculative selling totaled $19.5B, with $8B in the final week.
Of the final week's $8B, $5.2B was long liquidation and $2.8B was fresh shorts. Other and Non-Reportable traders made up about 95% of the latest selling.

Before the squeeze, options showed heavy demand for downside protection. Three-month implied vol was rising and normalized 25-delta put-call skew was at its 85th percentile over the past year (per Goldman's Quinn).

CTAs held sizeable gold shorts going into the squeeze. Some has likely been covered, which added fuel. How much short-covering remains is an open question, and the reset does not guarantee follow-through.

Goldman flags a sharp pickup in Chinese activity, with traders buying gold and selling copper. GS reads it as an expression of concern about the AI investment cycle, not a broader exit from equities, and warns the trade is increasingly dangerous and vulnerable to reversal.
Gold open interest is flat because short covering is offset by fresh longs, and volumes are still relatively light.

Goldman's Privorotsky argues gold may have become an inverse oil trade: soaring energy bills may have forced emerging-market central banks to sell or pause gold purchases, and falling oil eases that pressure. The theory is unproven.
Trade implication from Goldman: long gold may be a more attractive de-escalation trade than short oil, since much geopolitical premium has already come out of crude.
TME says gold is a poor fear hedge and tends to rally when fear falls. VIX remains the preferred global fear hedge.
Gold and the dollar are in a tight inverse relationship. Dollar weakness has been a tailwind for the squeeze, and DXY is the indicator to watch for whether it continues.
SocGen says Tether has accumulated 87.5 tonnes of gold since 2023, making it the fifth-largest net buyer globally, behind three central banks and one ETF.
Tether's gold holdings have grown at an annualized 31% since early 2023, against 13.6% for ETFs and 1.8% for central banks.

SocGen estimates Tether held 146.5 tonnes of physical gold as of June, comparable to Libya and ahead of the Philippines, and could reach 161 tonnes by September, equal to the seventh-largest gold ETF.

Technically, gold is back above the short-term trend line in place since late August but needs to reclaim the 50-day MA ($4,205) for a more persistent bullish move. The 200-day MA sits just below $4,500.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold must reclaim this level to establish a more persistent bullish move.
Remains well above current gold prices, so the longer-term trend is still unconfirmed.

tension_points.bull_case: The positioning flush removed speculative selling pressure, and falling oil, dollar weakness, Chinese demand and Tether's structural buying add support.
tension_points.bear_case: The move may be mostly short covering rather than fresh buying. Open interest is flat, volumes are light, and gold remains below the 50-day and 200-day MAs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to reclaim the 50-day MA ($4,205) and sustain the recovery.
